messages:
maria: FYI the re-encrypt orchestrator started failing ~2h ago with KMS throttling spikes across us-west-2 and europe-west1. We have ~10% of jobs in ERROR state. Any quick mitigations before we dig into root cause? :grimacing:

aj: Can you paste a sample error from the logs? sounds like RateExceeded/ThrottlingException from KMS.

maria: sure — snippet from the worker logs:

```
2026-02-18T14:12:03Z ERROR rewrap job=shard-14 key=ark-old-123 error=ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
stack: github.com/redwood/infer/rewrap/worker.process(…)
```

aj: yep classic. Two immediate mitigations: 1) reduce per-shard concurrency, 2) enable per-region token-bucket throttle in the orchestrator so we don't blast regional KMS quotas.

devon: also check if any misconfigured retries are spinning. If we have aggressive retry + high concurrency we amplify the cold throttles.

oliver: quick check: are we using ReEncrypt (server-side) where supported (AWS KMS ReEncrypt) or decrypt/encrypt data-key flows? ReEncrypt is fewer round trips but still counts against quota.

maria: we're doing decrypt-encrypt path for GCP and Azure (no server-side rewrap), AWS uses ReEncrypt for compatible keys.

security-bot: audit note: remember to keep audit-log entries for each rewrap action (principal, key id, oldKeyVersion, newKeyVersion, result). We saw gaps in week-of-02/05 where Cloud Audit Logs had missing entries for a subset of workers.

aj: action plan for now: patch deploy to reduce default shard parallelism from 8 -> 2, enable exponential backoff with jitter (cap at ~30s), and add a soft rate limiter per-region. I'll put up a PR.

maria: sounds good. any thoughts on checkpointing so partial successes don't get reprocessed? we had duplicate rewraps showing up in the runbook.

devon: we should checkpoint at the per-object level in the metadata store. current job commits only after the entire file group. Change to per-object atomic mark + idempotent rewrap by writing new envelope with a deterministic header. That way retries are safe.

kevin: for GCP/AKV we must ensure service accounts have both decrypt and encrypt on the key versions. I found a few service accounts missing the `cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` role — that shows up as AccessDenied not Throttling, but validate now while we reduce concurrency.

oliver: also consider backoff-aware batching: group small objects into a single KMS call where possible (i.e., multi-rewrap transaction by re-encrypting a single data key for a batch). That reduces calls but increases blast radius if a batch fails. trade-offs.

maria: AJ — can you add a metric emit for KMS 429/Throttling per-region and send alert if >50/min? right now we only have a generic 5xx counter.

aj: will do. Also adding a debug endpoint to show current token-bucket status per-region so SRE can tune concurrency without redeploy.

sre-oncall: once you throttle, please deploy the limiter config first and then scale down consumers. We'll be standing by to reduce autoscaling targets on the worker deployment.

devon: for error recovery strategy: categorize errors into transient (throttling, 5xx), permanent (AccessDenied, KeyDisabled), and partial (some items succeed). For transient — exponential retry -> move to DLQ after N attempts, alert. For permanent — stop shard, escalate via PagerDuty.

maria: what about audit / compliance: we need a tamper-evident trail proving rewrap happened and which key version encrypted each envelope. Can we dump a signed manifest after each successful batch?

security-bot: suggestion: write a manifest file to GCS/S3 signed with our deployment key and store a hash in the audit ledger (BigTable/Dynamo). Include oldKeyVersion/newKeyVersion, object IDs, timestamp, operator. That satisfies auditors who ask for proof-of-rotation.

kevin: note on Azure Key Vault: rewrap uses `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` and there's a per-key request limit that is different from AWS/GCP. We should maintain per-provider throttle knobs and default them to conservative values.

oliver: small config example for orchestrator token bucket and retry policy:

```yaml
rewrap:
  concurrency_per_shard: 2
  per_region_token_bucket:
    us-west-2: { capacity: 100, refill_qps: 10 }
    europe-west1: { capacity: 80, refill_qps: 8 }
  retry_policy: { base_ms: 200, max_ms: 30000, max_retries: 6, jitter: true }
  dlq: s3://rewrap-dlq/failed-objects/
```

devon: +1. also add a `checkpoint_interval` so long-running shards commit progress every N objects to the metadata store. Use idempotent writes for safety.

maria: I'll run a controlled canary over a small customer cohort in eu-west1 after the patch. Will post results in ~1h.

aj: ping me when canary starts, I'll watch KMS throttle metrics and temporarily pause canary if we spike.

maria: canary results: ~5% error (was 10%), KMS 429s down from 70/min -> 12/min after lowering concurrency. Checkpointing prevented duplicate rewraps. Rolling out patch to remaining shards now.

sre-oncall: monitoring in place. merging the rate knobs to prod config. Follow-up: schedule a post-mortem to document root cause and any quota requests with cloud providers.

maria: thanks all. follow-up items: (1) PR for limiter + retry (aj), (2) per-object checkpointing design doc (devon), (3) audit manifest prototype (kevin/security-bot), (4) postmortem + quota requests (sre-oncall). Closing thread once PRs linked here. :white_check_mark:
